 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Ryan Day had no plans of revealing his starting quarterback Wednesday evening.
 The Ohio State coach said that both Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair would be prepared to play against USC on Saturday night. The trip to Los Angeles is the No. 2 Buckeyes' first game since Julian Sayin suffered a likely season-ending shoulder injury against No. 4 Indiana.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I'm not going to," Day said when asked if he was going to name a starting quarterback. "But both guys had a good week of practice and I think both will be ready to play. And I think guys on the team have confidence that if both were put into the game they can do their job. So we'll keep preparing and we'll see how Saturday goes."
 Fahey, a freshman, has served as Ohio State's No. 2 QB in 2026 and entered the Indiana game after Sayin's injury. His two pass attempts fell incomplete as Ohio State was incredibly conservative with a late lead.
 The Indiana game was Fahey's fourth appearance overall and featured his first meaningful snaps of the season. He's 9-of-13 passing for 203 yards and two touchdowns with two interceptions.
 St. Clair, a redshirt freshman, has appeared in two games and is 5-of-7 passing for 52 yards with a TD and an interception.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Every time you find yourself with a new quarterback and you go through that experience, you learn about what that is and there's things that you feel that you do right and things you can do better," Day said. "And you try to do the best you can to put them in the situation to be successful and win the game.
 "Ultimately that's the No. 1 thing, is win the game. And that's really what we're going to focus on. And I think within the game plan it's our job to have things where we can find him into a rhythm or if he's not in a rhythm we can get him into a rhythm and then if things are going well, ways to be aggressive — kind of back and forth, leaning on the guys around him."
 Sayin isn't the only key piece of the Ohio State offense that will be out on Saturday, either. Ja'Kobi Jackson had foot surgery after suffering an injury vs. Maryland and could be out for the rest of the regular season. Bo Jackson was the team's top back against Indiana, while Isaiah West got six carries.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A win at USC will keep Ohio State tied with UCLA at the top of the Big Ten and at least a game ahead of everyone else. The Bruins play their final non-conference game of the season against Nevada in Week 9, while four teams enter the weekend with one conference loss and USC is among six teams with two conference losses.
